status: STILL-OPEN (v3 fixed the type-owner, but the data SOURCE for /dashboard.json is still wrong)
description: v3 R6 (behavioral-spec.md:49-53) correctly aligns the UI owner with the real code: EmpireDashboard.tsx has its own local DashboardData and fetches /dashboard.json (EmpireDashboard.tsx:52-56,64-76). BUT the spec asserts the leaderboard arrives via 'its existing /dashboard.json fetch' (behavioral-spec.md:53) while the actual /dashboard.json that EmpireDashboard reads (apps/landing/public/dashboard.json) is a STATIC file whose shape is {updated_at, mrr, followers, views, spend, goals, basic_income, socials, lineage, ...} — it contains NO 'leaderboard' and NO 'total_net_worth_usd'. The aggregate's 'leaderboard' key is produced only by the netlify function dashboard-sync.js (dashboard-sync.js:14 returns aggregate(rows) from the Supabase 'instances' table) and is served at the FUNCTION endpoint, not at /dashboard.json (no netlify rewrite from /dashboard.json to the function exists). So extending EmpireDashboard's local type with leaderboard?: LeaderboardEntry[] adds a field the fetched file never contains; the on-chain leaderboard never reaches the UI. The spec's pipeline (behavioral-spec.md:21-23) and R6 never reconcile (a) which producer writes 'leaderboard' into the static /dashboard.json, (b) that the static file is sourced from instance-state by a Dais-owned sync (per project CLAUDE.md) — a DIFFERENT data source than the Supabase 'instances' table that feeds aggregate.

crossEvidence.note: netlify function returns aggregate(rows) (with leaderboard) at the FUNCTION endpoint, sourced from Supabase instances — not /dashboard.json
EmpireDashboard reads data.mrr.total_usd / data.goals.* — the static-file shape, which aggregate does NOT emit

fix: Name the single producer that writes 'leaderboard' into the exact /dashboard.json EmpireDashboard fetches, and reconcile the two data sources (Supabase instances vs Dais-owned instance-state render). Either (a) have the Dais-owned dashboard-sync merge aggregate(enrichOnChain(...)).leaderboard into the static /dashboard.json, or (b) point EmpireDashboard at the function endpoint. State this in the spec and add a proof that the consumed file actually carries leaderboard.
